extracted.intended_audience: corporate clients, startups, inventors, and procurement/legal teams evaluating or selecting U.S. patent prosecution counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing a law firm's U.S. patent prosecution practice by the substantive services, capabilities, and outcomes it offers (portfolio strategy, examiner engagement, post-grant proceedings, technical depth, deal/monetization support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop patent portfolios aligned with client strategic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: We actively develop patent portfolios to achieve our clients’ strategic goals, whether they are focused on defensive coverage, licensing revenue, creating barriers to market entry, preparation for litigation, monetizing non-essential patent assets, or building value for a strategic exit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether prosecution is driven by a stated business strategy (defense, licensing, litigation, monetization, exit). The page lists explicit strategic goals to align portfolios with; look for tailored portfolio priorities rather than one-size-fits-all filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution beyond procedural compliance (creative, proactive approaches)
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t just go through the motions of patent prosecution. By thinking outside of the box, we stress creative and proactive approaches to accelerating and improving prosecution results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether counsel offers proactive strategies (e.g., creative claim drafting, tactical filings, accelerated prosecution techniques) rather than merely responding to office actions. Examples: participation in pilot programs, examiner meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face-to-face examiner engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Often meeting face-to-face with U.S. Patent Examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the firm regularly conducts examiner interviews/face-to-face engagement as part of its prosecution strategy to improve allowance prospects and speed—an emphasized tactic on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and scientific depth of attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Our attorneys have strong technical and scientific backgrounds that enable us to deeply understand the details of our clients’ technologies, which allow us to craft an individualized patent strategy for each client. Many have doctoral, medical, or masters degrees, and many have years of industry experience prior to becoming an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the technical credentials and industry experience of prosecution attorneys as a factor in their ability to understand inventions, draft claims, and interact with examiners and clients. Specialized degrees and prior industry work are cited as important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized patent strategy for each client
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong technical understanding allows us to craft an individualized patent strategy for each client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of tailored strategies (rather than cookie-cutter filing), e.g., claims and filing pathways that reflect client business objectives and technology specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-functional prosecution and litigation teams
rubrics_metrics.description: We have created a number of cross-functional teams where patent prosecution and litigation attorneys work closely with each other, crafting multi-dimensional tactics and strategies that take into account our clients’ business goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether prosecution is coordinated with litigation counsel to produce patents that are both strong before the Office and in enforcement/defense. The page highlights hybrid teams as a specific structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating patents that support stronger litigation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: These hybrid teams are able to create stronger patents in the patent office that lead to better litigation results as well as greater insight into defending against patent lawsuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the firm's emphasis on drafting and prosecution choices that anticipate litigation (e.g., claim breadth vs. enforceability, evidence preservation). Look for stated benefits linking prosecution decisions to courtroom performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation in post-grant proceedings under the AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: The hybrid teams also play an essential role in representing our clients in the new post-grant proceedings instituted under the America Invents Act (AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify experience in inter partes review (IPR), post-grant review (PGR), covered business method reviews, and other AIA-era proceedings. The firm positions post-grant experience as a core prosecution-related capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic handling of quasi‑litigation proceedings before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Our teams of litigators and patent prosecutors work synergistically to develop strategies to navigate these quasi-litigation proceedings before the U.S. Patent Office – either to defend a client from an invalidity challenge of its patent or to develop a strategy for challenging a competitor’s patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to provide both offensive and defensive strategies in USPTO post-grant venues, including integrated prosecution-litigation planning for challenges and defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding business realities and industry trends
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to understand the business realities surrounding the intellectual property. This holistic view of the legal landscape, our clients’ interests and overall industry trends give us a greater understanding of how inventions are implemented and used, as well as the direction technology itself is headed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether counsel situates patent strategy within market, regulatory, and industry contexts. The firm emphasizes holistic, business-aware prosecution advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop technology protection strategies and risk identification
rubrics_metrics.description: With the insight gleaned, we are able to quickly develop successful technology protection strategies [and] identify potential risks to avoid third-party action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for proactive risk analysis (e.g., freedom-to-operate, third-party rights) and tailored protection plans. The page frames this as an outcome of business/technical understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence for acquisitions and portfolio management tied to exits
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct diligence associated with acquisitions, and create prosecution portfolio management strategies tailored around individual exit plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure experience doing IP due diligence for M&A, and ability to shape prosecution and portfolio structure to maximize exit value (e.g., claim scope, geographic coverage, term management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience with patent term adjustments and extensions (35 U.S.C. §156 and PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The firm obtained five years of Patent Term Extension for the key Abreva patent for regulatory delays under 35 U.S.C. 156, and filed suit against the U.S. Patent Office on behalf of a client to maximize patent term adjustment awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate counsel’s track record and tactics for securing patent term extensions and adjustments (including litigation when necessary). Specific statutory mechanisms (35 U.S.C. 156 for PTE, PTA disputes) are cited as capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of commercialization outcomes (licenses, acquisitions, royalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative engagements show successful license negotiations resulting in millions in royalties, and client acquisitions (e.g., Skybox to Google, IDev to Abbott, Ulthera acquisition) tied to patent portfolio development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider concrete business outcomes achieved through prosecution (license deals, royalty streams, M&A) as evidence of effective IP strategy and monetization support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to secure patents in challenging circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: After other law firms were unable to convince the U.S. Patent Office as to patentability of the Horst Link suspension, Knobbe Martens was successful in securing three patents for the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether counsel has experience overcoming difficult rejections or convincing examiners where others failed—an indicator of prosecution skill and persistence.
